dial.summary: 4/8 indicators supportive on November 14 — BTC.D holding firm at ~59% and near-zero/negative perp funding rates (0.0052%, reports of negative on major exchanges) signal healthy deleveraging rather than panic, keeping accumulation conditions intact despite BTC falling to ~$67–69K; ISM Manufacturing at 55.5 and Global M2 expanding at $104.3T sustain the macro bid, but DXY elevated at 103.28 and real yields shifting to flat/elevated (2.86%, now neutral) represent the primary headwinds; stablecoin dominance jump to 12.5% (from 11.0%) reflects risk-off repositioning within crypto rather than macro breakdown.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) holds at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317.08B per MacroMicro series); October G4 data not yet published as of November 14, 2026 — MacroMicro typically updates mid-month following the reference month, so October G4 update expected mid-to-late November 2026; US M2 at $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per Macrotrends/FRED H.6); August G4 aggregate was $103.66T, confirming Sep ($104.3T) as an increase; 4-week Aug→Sep change +$0.64T (+0.6%) exceeds flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged from Nov 13 run — October G4 data publication pending.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.6%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0, New Orders 55.5, Backlog of Orders 56.4, Prices Paid 77.9 (up from 71.1 in August — persistent inflationary pressure in manufacturing); August was 55.6, September 54.5, October 55.5; 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value unchanged — October 55.5 is the current monthly reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 103.28 as of November 13, 2026 close (GuruFocus: 103.278; Trading Economics: 103.147); intraday Nov 14 pre-open ranged 103.06–103.44 (Dealplexus 03:29 IST); Nov 12 close was 102.85 (+0.63% on hot CPI/hawkish Fed repricing per Vantage Markets); 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 14 to 103.28 on November 13, net +~1.5–1.8%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted — ICE spot corroborated via GuruFocus and Trading Economics.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.86% on November 12, 2026 (FRED series last updated Nov 13 at 3:16 PM CST; Nov 13 observation scheduled for release Nov 16); prior readings: Nov 10: 2.78% (hot-CPI-driven +12bps from Nov 9's 2.66%), Nov 9: 2.66%, Nov 6: 2.63%; real yields rose 8bps from 2.78% (Nov 10) to 2.86% (Nov 12) as Treasury market repriced December FOMC hike odds further; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately 2.85–2.90% on October 14 (Oct 5 high: 2.95%) to 2.86% on November 12, net change approximately 0 to -4bps, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (above 2% but flat trend — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2%; supportive requires falling or below 1%; neither condition fully met); 10Y nominal 5.10–5.15%, breakeven ~2.24–2.29%.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at approximately +27bps as of November 13, 2026 close (CappNotes closing note: 10Y at 5.15%, 2Y at 4.88%; Le Private Banker Nov 12: +24bps with 10Y 5.10%, 2Y 4.86%; yieldcurve.pro Nov 10: +25bps); 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +28–32bps on October 14 to +27bps on November 13, net change approximately -1 to -5bps within flat threshold; long-end yields rose faster than short-end on Nov 13 as term premium widened slightly; 52-week range 20–74bps; status neutral (positive spread, no sustained steepening, not deeply inverted — headwind requires < -50bps which is far away); next major inflection to watch: December 9 FOMC decision impact on 2Y repricing.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,758,867M ($6.759T) for week ended November 11, 2026 (H.4.1 released November 12, 2026 per Federal Reserve; +$10,722M WoW from Nov 4's $6,748,145M, +$178,405M YoY); prior weekly readings: Nov 4 $6,748,145M, Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week change Oct 14 → Nov 11: +$3,228M (~+$3.2B, essentially flat); balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +$178.4B (+2.7%); status supportive (flat with slight growth, no aggressive QT — zero eliminations per H.4.1 header confirms figure matches WALCL); value updated to $6.76T reflecting Nov 11 H.4.1 release.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC perp funding rate 0.0052% (~5.7% annualized) as of November 13–14, 2026 snapshot vs 0.0100% base; Brave New Coin reports negative funding on Binance, OKX, and Bybit on November 13 (short traders paying longs), consistent with deleveraging; The Block 7DMA APY: 8.04% as of Nov 12 (down 0.34pp in 24h); prior readings: 0.0098% (Nov 13 morning), 0.0069% (Nov 12 OI-weighted), 0.0087% (Nov 8); BTC at ~$67–69K (down ~6% over 2 days) with liquidations $700M+ in 24h (92% longs per CoinGlass Nov 13–14); 30-day trend FLAT — mid-October rates were near zero/slightly negative, now 0.0052%, within flat noise range; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold); near-zero/negative funding on major exchanges is a classic accumulation signal — no overleveraged long exposure despite recent BTC pullback.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $285.585B as of November 13, 2026 (DefiLlama: USDT $175.516B, USDC $69.447B); total crypto market cap ~$2.29–2.33T as of November 14, 2026 05:02 UTC (TokenPost: $2.29T; CMC via CryptoPotato: $2.33T); implied stablecoin dominance ~12.3–12.5% (using $285.585B / $2.31T midpoint); prior: 11.0% on Nov 13 (when TOTAL was ~$2.41–2.60T); 30-day trend UP — October 13 dominance ~10.5–10.8%, November 10 at 11.40–11.51% (Au79 Macro), now ~12.5%; BTC.D at ~58.8–59.3% (TokenPost/CryptoPotato), BTC at $66,957–69,031; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL has DECLINED from $2.60T to $2.29T (not rising), so headwind condition not met; supportive condition (falling dominance) also not met; rise in dominance reflects risk-off repositioning as BTC falls, but TOTAL contraction prevents headwind classification.

upcoming.title: US Retail Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey at 8:30 AM ET; September retail sales were +0.8% MoM (well above the +0.3% forecast); a print above +0.5% MoM would add to the already-strong December 9 FOMC hike case after the hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, released Nov 10) and October PPI (released Nov 13); DXY at 103.28 (52-week range top) reflects persistent inflation pressure; a miss near 0% would add soft-landing ambiguity but is unlikely to outweigh the inflation surprise given DXY elevated; this is among the last major growth reads before the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period ahead of the December 9 decision.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases October 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17) at 9:15 AM ET; September industrial production rose +0.4% MoM; a continued expansion would corroborate the October ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); Fed plans an annual G.17 revision release on November 24, so this reading may be subject to revision; released same day as October Retail Sales.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 New Residential Construction at 8:30 AM ET; elevated mortgage rates (30Y near 7.1%) and real yields at 2.86% (flat on 4-week basis but historically high) continue to pressure housing affordability; after the hot CPI print sealing higher-for-longer expectations, a sharp drop in permits would underscore the housing drag on Q4 2026 growth.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes — October 27–28 Meeting
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% (vote 10–2) at that meeting; minutes will reveal member views on the threshold for a December 9 hike given elevated ISM Prices Paid (77.9 in October per November 2 release) and Iran-war supply shocks; both October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10) and October PPI (released Nov 13) arrived after the October meeting — markets will read the minutes against the new inflation reality; FOMC blackout period begins ~November 29 ahead of the December 9 decision.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET on Thursday November 19; final weekly labor read before Thanksgiving and the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period; a sustained trend above 220K would pressure December 9 hike odds given the already-hot CPI (+0.4% MoM Oct) and elevated DXY (103.28); next NFP release is December 4 (November data), arriving just 5 days before the December 9 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia releases November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey at 8:30 AM ET; provides a first-look at November manufacturing activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a positive print above 0 would reinforce the October ISM signal at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); released on the third Thursday of the month, same day as jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Existing Home Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: National Association of Realtors releases October 2026 Existing Home Sales at 10:00 AM ET; mortgage rates near 7.1% continue to suppress turnover via the low-rate lock-in effect; provides a full-month housing transaction count for October; real yields holding at 2.86% (flat on 4-week basis) keep affordability severely constrained; watch for any inventory normalization trends.
